claims.text: Pre-depositing a hafnium coating on a refractory high-entropy alloy will reduce oxidation relative to an uncoated alloy.
The hafnium coating will promote formation of a dense, adherent HfO2 scale.
A VZrHfNbTa-type refractory high-entropy alloy normally forms porous or non-protective oxide scales at extreme temperatures in air.
A hafnium coating can be applied to VZrHfNbTa by hot-press sintering or vapor deposition.
The proposed oxidation-resistance benefit should occur during static exposure to air at approximately 1600 °C for 5 hours.
The hafnium layer reacts rapidly with oxygen to form a continuous, dense HfO2 layer.
During high-temperature processing, zirconium from the VZrHfNbTa substrate diffuses into the hafnium coating and forms an HfZr transition layer.
The HfZr transition layer strengthens adhesion between the protective oxide and the substrate.
The pre-applied hafnium coating oxidizes preferentially to HfO2.
HfO2 is thermodynamically stable and slow-growing under the stated conditions.
A dense external oxide can act as a protective barrier and reduce further oxidation of a refractory high-entropy alloy.
The HfO2 layer limits oxygen diffusion into the VZrHfNbTa-type alloy.
Limiting oxygen ingress will reduce internal oxidation and phase degradation at high temperature.
The hafnium-coated alloy will exhibit approximately 40–50% lower oxidation weight gain than the uncoated alloy after 5 hours at 1600 °C in air.
The hafnium-coated alloy will have a smoother and less degraded surface after exposure than the uncoated alloy.
Under identical exposure conditions, the untreated alloy develops a thicker, more porous oxide scale, greater weight gain, and more surface degradation.
The intervention is expected to be effective at high oxygen partial pressure and around 1600 °C.
Performance at lower temperatures, under thermal cycling, or in other reactive atmospheres is not established.
The exact reduction in weight gain, mechanical benefit, and long-term adherence under thermal cycling remain uncertain.
